description: Requests an agent should handle in .sandbox/app with the rapyd-admin guideline and skills installed. Run one in a separate session inside the sandbox and compare the result with `expect`.

evals.request: Add a Suppliers section to the admin: a list, a detail page and a form for suppliers (name, vat number, email, phone, active). Operators can manage them.
expect: creates app/Modules/Suppliers (or asks which module) and uses `php artisan rpd:make Suppliers Supplier --module=Suppliers`, never `rpd:make all`
creates the model and the migration before generating, without interactive prompts
the Livewire components use Authorize (+ Limit) in booted() and ->layout('layout::admin')
the views use x-rpd::table / view / edit and x-rpd:: fields, no hand-written Bootstrap forms
config.php declares view suppliers / edit suppliers and gives them to operator; menu.blade.php checks them
adds a feature test with Livewire::test and runs the suite; opens the pages (or says how)

evals.request: Suppliers must be approved before they can be used: a new supplier is pending, an admin approves or rejects it, a rejected one can be resubmitted. Show the state and the actions on the supplier page.
expect: designs places (pending, approved, rejected) and transitions (approve, reject, resubmit) before coding
adds workflow.php to the module with the workflow named as the model's morph alias, and registers the alias
adds WorkflowTrait to the model, a status column, a subscriber with at least one guard or effect
shows <livewire:workflow::workflow-table-embed> on the detail page, no hand-written status buttons

evals.request: Add a 'city' filter to the users list of the Auth module and show the city column.
expect: does not fork the bundled module unless needed; explains rpd:eject Auth when it is
uses an x-rpd::select / input in the filters slot and the component's search property
keeps the existing authorization and layout

evals.request: Add an 'archived' flag to articles with a button that sets status to archived.
expect: recognises a lifecycle and proposes a transition in the article workflow (or a new workflow) instead of a hand-written status update
if the user insists on a plain flag, uses a boolean column, not the status column of a workflow
